title: Compact snapshot-led caching configurator for mixed-workload consoles
creator: Ava Kim
description: Design a compact, snapshot-driven UI panel that lets operators create, preview, and apply caching + batching policies for mixed workloads (short chat bursts, long-form generation, and embeddings-heavy routes). The panel should: provide clear recommendations derived from historical request snapshots; surface guardrail warnings when suggested settings could violate latency SLOs or increase token cost >10%; allow rapid simulation of expected cost/latency trade-offs; and include an easy rollback/preview flow tied to rollout policies. This is intended for Console -> Routes -> Performance tab as a collapsible card called 'Snapshot Configurator'.
background: Current Console configurators are verbose and split across screens: one for batching presets, one for KV cache toggles, and a separate recommendations panel. Operators ask for a compact surface to iterate quickly on live traffic patterns without context-switching. PM metrics show friction when converting recommendations into applied policies (12% drop-off). Engineering supports a lightweight API to fetch anonymized snapshots and run a simulated cost/latency model, enabling an in-console preview.
goals: Unify batching and cache settings into a one-panel workflow
Make recommendations actionable with one-click apply and staged rollout
Provide a cost/latency preview based on sampled snapshots
Surface deterministic guardrail warnings and remediation hints
non_goals: Changing runtime defaults or server-side enforcement
Replacing advanced optimizer UX in dedicated admin screens
proposed_flow: 1) User opens Route -> Performance -> Snapshot Configurator. 2) System shows top-3 snapshot clusters (by frequency/latency). 3) Designer selects a cluster; recommendations populate (batch size, prefix cache TTL, cache scope). 4) Inline cost/latency preview updates. 5) User tweaks sliders or chooses 'Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive' presets. 6) Guardrail banner appears if risk detected with remediation suggestion. 7) User clicks 'Apply as canary' or 'Apply to route'. 8) Console creates rollout with linked audit log and rollback button.
design_notes:
- Prioritize a single-row compact card for quick scanning.
- Use color-coded severity chips for guardrails (info/warn/error).
- Show token cost delta as absolute and percentage.
- Provide explicit link to 'why this recommendation' (small modal with snapshot examples).
- Keyboard-accessible sliders and ARIA labels for screen readers.
- Localize strings via i18n keys: console.snapshot_configurator.*
tradeoffs: We compress a lot of controls into a compact UI to reduce friction, which risks hiding advanced knobs. To mitigate, include 'Advanced' toggle that expands full policy JSON. Simulating cost/latency is an approximation — we annotate uncertainty bands and do not present exact guarantees.
alternatives_considered: Keep separate recommendation and config screens (current) — rejected due to friction
Full-width simulator with detailed histograms — deferred to optimizer-studio
CLI-first approach (engineers only) — not aligned with console self-serve goal
accessibility_considerations: Ensure contrast ratios meet AA, all controls reachable by keyboard, and live region updates for preview numbers to announce changes. Provide text-only summary of recommendation for screen readers.
tasks: Prototype Figma interactive states for presets and guardrails
Implement localization keys and copy review
Handoff to eng with acceptance criteria and component tokens
acceptance_criteria: Compact Snapshot Configurator card appears under Route -> Performance and follows visual spec
Selecting a snapshot cluster populates recommendation fields within 300ms (simulated)
Preview displays token cost delta and 95th latency estimate with uncertainty band
Applying as canary creates rollout entry in console with audit log link
Guardrail warnings appear for risk cases with clear remediation text
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: operators may over-rely on approximate simulation and misconfigure for tail latency. Mitigation: show uncertainty bands, recommend conservative preset by default, and add educational tooltip linking to docs. Risk: performance of in-console preview could add load to analytics backend. Mitigation: sample rate + cached previews and circuit-breaker after N requests.
